name: Abstract Motion Graphics
visualIdentity: A continuous, restrained system built from a few geometric shapes and limited colors. Deliberate proportions and centers of gravity unify repetition, division, merging, and rotation; each state should lead into the next.
suitableUses: Strongest as a self-contained shape system. Explicit fits include UI and product storytelling, editorial or minimalist layouts, motion posters, and staged geometric compositions. Brand idents, loops, section transitions, music visuals, and event openers are suggested uses. These are suitability cues, not requirements.
limitations: Avoid unrelated particles and light effects that weaken the motif. Adapt or omit recomposition when it obscures the subject, crops important details, forces text into unsafe areas, or disrupts page layout. Pinning must not block content or make video depend on scroll. Avoid chapter handoffs that obscure causality, violate continuity, or add no narrative value. Do not imply physical fluid behavior from simulated forms.
palette: Use few geometric forms and a limited coherent system. Optional fallback tokens for new artwork only: background #F6F0E2, foreground #283D47, accent_1 #458784, accent_2 #D28456; gradients are disabled. Exact task or approved brand/reference colors and role assignments take precedence; do not recolor assets or automatically alter or expand approved colors. Keep accents subordinate. Suggested opaque background/foreground text pairing has 9.997 contrast; accents are decorative and the cited accent pairs miss the 4.5 normal-text target. Recheck actual composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Repeat, divide, merge, rotate, and vary timing so states connect coherently. Preserve authored cuts, impacts, constant-speed passages, and reading holds. Optional motifs include contour-matched morphs with stable shape-family color roles, music-paced density changes from a precomputed beat map, or a fixed hero stage whose inner layout recomposes continuously. Interactive HTML may map finite scroll progress to staged states, chapter handoffs, or story steps; release pins without jumps and support backward/direct seeking, keyboard, touch, and reduced motion. Video must use time-driven states, not live input. Audio-reactive visuals require verified precomputed analysis.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory layer is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and objective; honor supplied assets and explicit audio requirements. Leave space for speech and reading, synchronize to motion where useful, and avoid clipping or competing vocals. Beat-driven visuals should use a precomputed beat map.
assetRequirements: Use reusable shape groups and shared coordinates for repetition and assembly; use an existing path-interpolation library for complex morphs. Load approved assets and fonts before rendering, retain exact copy and source colors, and prepare deterministic or baked states where needed. Optional SVG, Canvas, Paper.js, p5.js, or geometry tools serve specific drawing/procedural needs; they are not required bundles. Delaunay meshes are unconstrained 2D and may bridge concavities or holes.
combinations: Works well alone. Optional style-100 contour morphs can give states traceable lineage; style-105 timing can tie density and division to music. Keep the core motif, centers of gravity, and color roles coherent; avoid fake morph crossfades, unrelated particles/glow, rapid beat flashing, or live randomness. Other motion patterns—pinned hero recomposition, chapter transitions, bounded orb deformation, and scroll storytelling—are optional and only fit when the scene and narrative support them.
productionApproach: Select the visual renderer and motion engine by style, scene, and fidelity; give each animated property one owner. SVG is recommended for shapes; GSAP for staggered, seekable motion. Other listed tools are optional and must preserve the style. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, synchronization, validation, and export pipeline; use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a requirement, and record why. Drive video layers from shared composition time; verify direct and backward seeks. For interactive output, add appropriate scroll/input adapters while retaining coherent static or reduced-motion states.
